dimensions.usefulness: Actionable value for educational and creative builders. 1: little demonstrated practical value; 5: useful for a defined task; 10: exceptional broadly actionable value.
dimensions.impact: Potential significance to AI development, grounded in evidence. 1: minor incremental change; 5: meaningful advance within a domain; 10: exceptional field-wide significance.
dimensions.novelty: Demonstrated differentiation, not promotional claims. 1: little demonstrated differentiation; 5: a meaningful distinctive capability; 10: exceptional new capability or approach.
dimensions.maturity: Documented readiness and reliability. 1: speculative or inaccessible; 5: usable with material limits; 10: extensively documented and demonstrably dependable. Do not infer reliability from benchmark scores alone.
dimensions.openness: Inspectability, licensing, portability and reproducibility. 1: closed, restrictive and difficult to inspect or migrate; 5: meaningful access with material constraints; 10: exceptionally open and reproducible with permissive documented terms.

rules: Rate each dimension as an integer from 1 to 10; explain every rating with evidence and uncertainty.
Label vendor performance claims and distinguish access to code, weights, data and training methods.
Two distinct agents must independently review the exact report, evidence and rubric hashes, without seeing one another's ratings.
Publish only two approvals using model gpt-6-astra at high effort. A difference greater than two points on any dimension blocks publication.
Public dimension scores are the arithmetic mean of the two ratings, rounded to one decimal. Overall is the mean of those dimension scores.
Independent runs of the same model are not independent experimental validation.
Final mean impact below 5 requires 1000 report-body words; 5 through 7 requires 2000; above 7 requires 3000. Each target allows ten percent variation.
